$comment: Qwen Code settings for the workshop. Copy to ~/.qwen/settings.json (user scope)
or to <project>/.qwen/settings.json (project scope).
JSON has no comments, so notes live here and in docs/05-qwen-code.md.
EDIT BEFORE USE:
1. env.WORKSHOP_LITELLM_KEY      -> must match LITELLM_MASTER_KEY in configs/litellm/.env
2. generationConfig.contextWindowSize -> must match the -c you gave llama.cpp.
TWO RULES THAT ARE EASY TO GET WRONG, both verified against the bundled docs:
* modelProviders merges by REPLACE, not by merge. A project-scope
.qwen/settings.json containing modelProviders DISCARDS this whole catalogue.
That is why this file belongs in USER scope (~/.qwen/settings.json).
* Provider entries are SEALED. Top-level model.generationConfig values --
including contextWindowSize -- are IGNORED for models defined in
modelProviders. Every setting must live inside the provider entry itself.
samplingParams is also atomic: if you set it, put everything you want in it.
Model ids below must match model_name entries in configs/litellm/config.yaml,
which in turn must match ids your llama-swap exposes.
NO mcpServers BLOCK HERE, DELIBERATELY. Get the local model answering a
question end to end FIRST -- an MCP server is a second system to install and
debug on top of everything else, and every server adds its tool schemas to
every request. On an 8192-token window that can eat the whole budget before
your prompt arrives, on the model size that is worst at tool calling.
When your stack works and you want one:
qwen mcp add context7 npx -- -y @upstash/context7-mcp
then run /context detail before and after to see what it cost you.
See docs/05-qwen-code.md#mcp-eats-your-context.
